subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Samir Joshi <samir@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks + quick recap ask

Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. Quick note to capture what we discussed and to make sure we’re aligned before we dig into numbers. High level: Finbot is looking at ways to bring down inference costs for our document-processing models while keeping latency tight for live customer workflows.

A few quick bullets from our side:
- Primary pain: token-level cost during peak ingestion (invoice parsing) — current unit cost ~3x our target.
- Latency: p95 on current hosted endpoints ~200–300ms depending on batch; target is ~100ms p95 for real-time flows.
- Current stack: models hosted on GCP (A100 instances, autoscaled endpoints), some local caching but mostly per-request cold starts.
- Open to model changes if quality stays the same; want to explore quantization and cheaper model variants.
- Compliance: must keep customer PII encrypted in transit & at rest; KMS-managed keys are required.

Can you send a short discovery recap with suggested next steps and what you’d need from us (usage snapshot, latency histograms, desired SLA)? Also curious about Redwood’s approach to batching/caching and whether you recommend prefix caching for our workload.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Joshi
Head of ML Platform, Finbot
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Joshi <samir@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks + quick recap ask

Samir —

Really appreciate the time this morning. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can move quickly. I’ve cc’d Ben (our solutions lead) so he can prepare a short POA and initial commercial outline once we validate the usage numbers.

Recap of pain & goals
- Cost pressure: current unit economics are ~3x target. Your stated goal: reduce per-token inference cost by ~40% (or get to within your target budget) while preserving model accuracy on parsing.
- Latency: target p95 <= 100ms for the real-time invoice parsing path. Occasional higher p95 during bursts noted.
- Reliability: need predictable tail latency during peak ingestion windows and ability to burst without large cost spikes.

Current stack (as discussed)
- GCP hosted endpoints (A100), autoscaling. Minimal persistent KV/prefix caching in front of endpoints. No production quantized models today.
- KMS for keys required — Redwood supports customer-managed KMS in Private/Dedicated, and hosted customers can integrate KMS for encryption at rest.

Where Redwood can help (short summary)
- Unit economics: smart batching + KV/prefix caching and model/quantization recommendations targeted to your sequence lengths can materially reduce per-token spend. Typical wins we’ve seen: 20–50% depending on cache hit rate and quantization tolerance.
- Latency: our serving runtime optimizes for p95 with continuous batching and aggressive scheduling; we can aim for <=100ms p95 on a tuned profile for your workload and target composition.
- Quantization: if quality holds, 8-bit quantization (with calibration) is often a good tradeoff. We’ll run AB tests on a holdout prompt set.

Success criteria (what success looks like to Finbot)
1) 40% reduction in per-token inference cost (or meet your target unit economics)
2) p95 <= 100ms on production-like traffic pattern
3) Transparent tracing and cost breakdown per route/model

Immediate next steps
- Finbot: share usage snapshot (7–30 day rolling), latency histograms, and a sample prompt set for quality checks. (Priya — can you attach the usage export?)
- Redwood: we’ll share an initial POA, high-level pricing range, and an SLA template for review. Ben will own the commercial side.
- Schedule: tech deep-dive (30–60min) next week to go over trace-level data and discuss caching strategy.

Attachments: I’m attaching our standard SLA template for initial review; Ben will follow up with a POA draft after we get the usage numbers.

If that all looks right, propose we schedule the tech deep-dive on Tuesday or Wednesday next week (I’m flexible after 10am PT).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Priya Nair <priya.nair@finbot.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Joshi <samir@finbot.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks + quick recap ask

Thanks Marissa — this looks great. I attached the 14-day usage export you requested (Finbot-usage-snapshot.csv). Highlights:
- Avg daily tokens: 28M (peak days up to 55M)
- Typical sequence length: 120–450 tokens (invoice OCR + context)
- Current average latency: 180ms; p95 spikes to ~320ms on peak minutes

Clarifications / asks:
- We are open to 8-bit quantization if the parsing accuracy on key fields (amount, date, vendor name) stays within 0.5% of baseline.
- We’d like to understand how prefix caching would fit with our per-document variable contexts (sometimes similar prefixes across invoices, other times unique).
- Trial: if you can run a 2-week pilot on a subset of traffic (say 10% routed to Redwood) to show cost/latency delta, that’d be ideal.

Attaching: Finbot-usage-snapshot.csv

— Priya
Priya Nair
Head of Engineering, Finbot
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Nair <priya.nair@finbot.ai>, Samir Joshi <samir@finbot.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks + quick recap ask

Priya — perfect, thanks for the snapshot and the notes. Quick next items so we can lock dates and owners: 

1) Tech deep-dive (Marissa + Ben + Redwood infra engs): propose Tuesday 2027-05-04 10:30am PT — agenda: review token distribution, p95 traces, talk through prefix/KV caching patterns and quantization plan. Please confirm or propose alternative.

2) Pilot scope: Finbot approves 10% traffic pilot — Redwood to provide routing config and POA. Ben will draft a POA and preliminary commercial range once we validate the snapshot.

3) Legal / security: we’ll send SLA-template.pdf for your legal review. We support KMS integrations — if you can share the KMS provider (GCP KMS or third-party) we’ll confirm specifics ahead of pilot.

Ben — can you draft the POA + pricing band (trial pricing and post-trial estimate) after you review the snapshot? I’ll lead the tech call and validate the quantization plan with infra.
